text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim against development","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a direct position early so the reader immediately knows the argument being made."},{"evidence":"three separate body paragraphs on danger, lawsuits, and laziness","quality":"organization","description":"It groups ideas into distinct points, making the essay easier to follow than a more blended response."},{"evidence":"“Having driverless cars can be dangerous...”; “they will cause problems”; “Americans are known for being lazy”","quality":"point development","description":"It develops each reason with a focused explanation rather than repeatedly circling the same idea."},{"evidence":"“who is at fault-the driver or the manufactuer?”","quality":"use of source evidence","description":"It includes a specific detail from the article to support the argument instead of relying only on opinion."},{"evidence":"“Having driverless cars is just more oppurtunity for us citizens to be able to wreck.”","quality":"reasoning","description":"It tries to connect evidence to a larger claim about consequences, showing more argumentative thinking."},{"evidence":"closing restatement of negative effects and recommendation to stick with regular cars","quality":"conclusion","description":"It ends by reinforcing the position and summarizing the main reasons in a more decisive way."}]}
